label: Pressure Reactivity Index 0
definition: An index representing the percentage of time pressure reactivity index is negative during monitoring.

label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Correction
definition: An adjustment applied to cerebral perfusion pressure values when the blood pressure transducer is not at tragus level.

label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Methodology
definition: The technical approach used to measure and calculate cerebral perfusion pressure, including transducer placement.

label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Range
definition: The span between minimum and maximum cerebral perfusion pressure values observed or recommended.

label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Target
definition: A specific intended or recommended value or range for cerebral perfusion pressure in clinical management.

label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Threshold
definition: A boundary value for cerebral perfusion pressure used to trigger clinical actions or define treatment goals.

label: Hypotension Risk
definition: The likelihood of a patient experiencing low blood pressure, assessed in clinical settings such as haemodialysis.

label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Safety Limits
definition: Boundaries for cerebral perfusion pressure considered safe to avoid secondary insults.

label: Demographic Variable
definition: A patient characteristic such as age or sex, used as input features in predictive modeling.

label: Intracranial Pressure Burden
definition: The cumulative dose of intracranial pressure exposure per patient, often defined as the percentage of time in the red zone.

label: Pupil Abnormalities
definition: Clinical findings involving abnormal pupil reactivity or size, indicating potential neurological compromise.

label: Hypotensive Events
definition: Episodes of low blood pressure, defined and graded for monitoring in clinical studies such as those using the EUSIG system.

label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Variability
definition: The degree of fluctuation or dispersion in cerebral perfusion pressure values over time or across individuals.

label: Intracranial Pressure Insult
definition: An episode of raised intracranial pressure characterized by specific intensity and duration thresholds, associated with neurological outcomes.

label: Therapy Intensity Level Scale
definition: A scale used to assess the intensity of intracranial pressure-lowering strategies in traumatic brain injury management.

label: Intracranial Pressure-time Burden
definition: The cumulative impact of intracranial pressure insults over time, visualized as an area under the curve above a threshold.

label: Therapy Intensity Level (TIL)
definition: A scoring system quantifying the intensity of therapeutic interventions in traumatic brain injury management.

label: Heart Rate Variability
definition: The variation in time intervals between heartbeats, used as a predictor of hypotension.

label: Glasgow Coma Scale Assessment
definition: A neurological scale used to assess the level of consciousness in patients, with scores obtained at admission to hospital and ICU.

label: Intracranial Hypertension Index 20
definition: An index representing the percentage of time intracranial pressure exceeds 20 mmHg during monitoring.

label: Pre-decompressive Craniectomy Period
definition: The time period before decompressive craniectomy surgery when monitoring data are collected.

label: Therapy Intensity Level Basic Scale
definition: A scale used to assess the intensity of intracranial pressure-lowering strategies before decompressive craniectomy.

label: Hypotension Warning Time
definition: The time interval before a predicted hypotensive event, with average values relevant in clinical decision thresholds.

label: Intracranial Hypertension Index 25
definition: An index representing the percentage of time intracranial pressure exceeds 25 mmHg during monitoring.

label: Intensive Care Unit Stay
definition: The period during which a patient is admitted to the intensive care unit for monitoring and treatment of severe conditions like traumatic brain injury.

label: Heart Rate Standard Deviation
definition: The variability of heart rate over time, calculated over sequential time windows as an input feature.

label: Intensive Care Unit
definition: A specialized hospital department providing intensive treatment and monitoring for critically ill patients, such as those with traumatic brain injury.

label: Refractory Elevated Intracranial Pressure
definition: Persistently high intracranial pressure that does not respond to standard medical therapies, often requiring surgical intervention.

label: Hypotension After Induction of General Anesthesia
definition: A drop in blood pressure occurring after the administration of general anesthesia, which can be predicted to improve patient safety.

label: Secondary Injury
definition: Additional brain damage occurring after the initial traumatic brain injury, often due to physiological insults like elevated intracranial pressure.

label: Therapy Intensity Level 4 Score
definition: A score measuring the intensity of therapeutic interventions in traumatic brain injury management.

label: Heart Rate Slope
definition: The rate of change of heart rate over time, calculated over sequential time windows as an input feature.

label: Second-tier Treatment
definition: More aggressive interventions applied when first-tier treatments fail to control intracranial pressure.

label: Aggressive Therapy
definition: Intensive medical interventions aimed at rapidly addressing severe conditions like elevated intracranial pressure.

label: Barbiturate Administration
definition: The administration of barbiturate drugs like thiopental as a third-tier intervention to reduce intracranial pressure in TBI.

label: Outcome Data
definition: Clinical assessments such as the Glasgow Outcome Scale collected at specified time points to evaluate patient recovery.

label: Therapeutic Actions
definition: Clinical interventions intended to treat raised intracranial pressure.

label: Patient Representatives
definition: Individuals, such as family members or legally authorized representatives, who participate in healthcare decisions on behalf of the patient.

label: Secondary Brain Injury
definition: Additional brain damage that occurs after the initial traumatic insult, often due to physiological insults like raised intracranial pressure.

label: Cerebral Hypoperfusion Index
definition: A metric quantifying periods of inadequate cerebral blood flow, used in monitoring brain injury patients.

label: Arterial Blood Pressure Transducer
definition: A medical device used to measure blood pressure invasively, placed at specific anatomical reference points.

label: Bifrontal Craniectomy
definition: A surgical procedure removing the frontal bones bilaterally to relieve intracranial pressure.

label: Cerebral Hypoperfusion Index 60
definition: An index representing the percentage of time cerebral perfusion pressure falls below 60 mmHg during monitoring.

label: Clinical Examination
definition: A physical assessment performed by healthcare providers to evaluate patient status.

label: Clinical Study
definition: A research study conducted in a clinical environment to evaluate predictive models, involving patient data collection.

label: Adult Patient
definition: A traumatic brain injury patient aged 16 years or older, included in the adult cohort of the study.

label: Arterial Oxygen Saturation
definition: Oxygen saturation measured in the blood, used as a physiological parameter to detect hypoxic events.

label: Median Cerebral Perfusion Pressure
definition: The median value of cerebral perfusion pressure measurements over a monitoring period for a patient or centre.

label: Third-tier Medical Therapy
definition: Advanced medical interventions including barbiturates used when first and second-tier treatments are insufficient.

label: Mean Cerebral Perfusion Pressure
definition: The average cerebral perfusion pressure calculated from monitoring data.

label: Mean Intracranial Pressure
definition: The average pressure inside the cranium, a key monitoring parameter in traumatic brain injury management.

label: Secondary Ischemic Damage
definition: Brain injury resulting from reduced blood flow and oxygen delivery following the initial traumatic insult.

label: Outcome Score
definition: A clinical assessment score used to evaluate patient outcomes, such as the Glasgow Outcome Score.

label: Cerebrovascular Pressure Autoregulation
definition: The physiological mechanism that maintains stable cerebral blood flow despite changes in perfusion pressure.

label: Total Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Range
definition: The full span of cerebral perfusion pressure values observed over a monitoring period, from minimum to maximum.

label: Inter-individual Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Variability
definition: Differences in cerebral perfusion pressure between different patients.

label: Physiological Vital Function
definition: Essential bodily functions that are extensively monitored in critical care settings.

label: Passive Autoregulation Insults
definition: Intracranial pressure insults occurring when cerebrovascular autoregulation is passive, affecting outcome associations.

label: Systemic Events
definition: Whole-body physiological occurrences that can influence cerebral perfusion pressure.

label: Cerebrovascular Pressure Reactivity
definition: The responsiveness of cerebral blood vessels to changes in perfusion pressure, used to determine optimal cerebral perfusion pressure.

label: Pressure and Time Burden
definition: A metric quantifying the extent and duration of intracranial pressure insults, used in the analysis of traumatic brain injury management.

label: Minute-by-minute Data
definition: High-frequency physiological monitoring data recorded every minute in traumatic brain injury patients.

label: Unfavourable Neurological Outcome
definition: A clinical outcome defined as death, vegetative state, or severe disability, corresponding to Glasgow Outcome Score categories 1-3.

label: Dynamic Individual Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Target
definition: A cerebral perfusion pressure goal tailored to an individual patient's autoregulation capacity.

label: Active Autoregulation Insults
definition: Intracranial pressure insults occurring when cerebrovascular autoregulation is active, affecting outcome associations.

label: Mean Pressure Reactivity Index
definition: The average pressure reactivity index calculated from monitoring data.

label: Blood Pressure Transducer
definition: A medical device used to measure arterial blood pressure, with placement at atrium level being a standard for accurate pressure measurement.

label: Monitoring Time
definition: The duration over which physiological parameters such as cerebral perfusion pressure are continuously recorded for a patient.

label: Mean Arterial Blood Pressure Slope
definition: The rate of change of mean arterial blood pressure over time, calculated over sequential time windows as an input feature.

label: Paediatric Patient
definition: A traumatic brain injury patient aged between 2 and 16 years, included in the paediatric cohort of the study.

label: Extracranial Injuries
definition: Injuries occurring outside the cranial vault, often associated with polytrauma in traumatic brain injury patients.

label: Haemodialysis Treatment
definition: A medical procedure used to filter waste and excess fluid from the blood in patients with kidney failure, during which hypotension can occur.

label: Physiological Threshold
definition: A critical value of a physiological parameter, such as intracranial pressure, used to guide clinical decisions.

label: Head-injured Patients
definition: Patients who have sustained traumatic brain injuries, often requiring intensive care monitoring and management.

label: Physiological Data
definition: Continuous measurements of vital signs and other bodily functions, used for monitoring and predictive analysis in clinical settings.

label: Neuro-icu
definition: A specialized intensive care unit for patients with neurological conditions such as traumatic brain injury.

label: Systolic Arterial Blood Pressure Slope
definition: The rate of change of systolic arterial blood pressure over time, calculated over sequential time windows as an input feature.

label: Neurological Deterioration
definition: Worsening of neurological function, which can be influenced by intracranial pressure and cerebral perfusion pressure.

label: Neurocognitive Scores
definition: Quantitative assessments of cognitive functions such as memory, attention, and executive function, used to evaluate neurological outcomes.

label: Severe Traumatic Brain Injury
definition: A severe form of traumatic brain injury characterized by significant neurological impairment, often with Glasgow Coma Scale scores of 8 or below.

label: Median Pressure Reactivity Index 0
definition: The median percentage of monitoring time with pressure reactivity index above 0.

label: Haemodialysis Patients
definition: Patients undergoing haemodialysis for kidney failure, who are monitored for risks such as hypotension.

label: Systolic Arterial Blood Pressure
definition: A physiological variable measuring the peak arterial pressure during cardiac contraction, used as an input feature for predictive modeling.

label: Standard Medical Treatment
definition: Conventional, non-surgical management strategies for conditions such as traumatic brain injury, typically involving medication and monitoring.

label: Peripheral Arterial Blood Pressure Waveform
definition: A physiological signal obtained from peripheral arteries, used for monitoring and predicting acute hypotensive episodes.

label: Active Insult
definition: An intracranial pressure insult classified based on a negative or zero average low-frequency autoregulation index, indicating impaired autoregulation.

label: Blood Pressure Measurement System
definition: Medical devices used to measure blood pressure, which can be sensitive to artifacts from patient movement or procedures.

label: Critical Care
definition: A medical specialty focused on the management of critically ill patients, often involving advanced monitoring and technology.

label: Baseline Risk Factor
definition: Patient characteristics such as age, gender, and admission neurological status that influence outcome in traumatic brain injury.

label: Cranioplasty
definition: A surgical procedure to repair a skull defect, often performed after decompressive craniectomy.

label: Median Intracranial Hypertension Index 20
definition: The median percentage of monitoring time with intracranial pressure above 20 mmHg.

label: Third-tier Intervention
definition: Advanced treatment options used when first and second-tier interventions fail in traumatic brain injury management.

label: Median Intracranial Hypertension Index 25
definition: The median percentage of monitoring time with intracranial pressure above 25 mmHg.

label: Traumatic Intracranial Hypertension
definition: A condition characterized by elevated intracranial pressure following traumatic brain injury, often requiring medical or surgical intervention.

label: Icp-lowering Treatment
definition: Therapies specifically designed to reduce elevated intracranial pressure.

label: Passive Insult
definition: An intracranial pressure insult classified based on a positive average low-frequency autoregulation index, indicating preserved autoregulation.

label: Paediatric Traumatic Brain Injury
definition: Traumatic brain injury occurring in children, studied as a distinct patient cohort.

label: Multimodality Monitoring
definition: The use of multiple monitoring techniques to assess various physiological parameters in critically ill patients.

label: Neurointensive Care
definition: Specialized intensive care unit management for patients with severe neurological injuries including traumatic brain injury.

label: Tragus Height
definition: The anatomical level of the external ear tragus, used as a reference point for blood pressure transducer placement.

label: Bilateral Fixed and Dilated Pupils
definition: A clinical sign indicating severe brain injury or herniation, characterized by unresponsive and enlarged pupils.

label: Sports Related Injury
definition: A type of traumatic injury related to sports activities, categorized under injury causes in the patient cohort.

label: Acute Hypotensive Episodes
definition: Sudden, severe drops in blood pressure that are critical to predict and manage in intensive care patients.

label: Traumatic Brain Injury
definition: A major health and socio-economic problem characterized by brain damage resulting from external trauma, associated with high mortality and morbidity rates.

label: Drug Responses
definition: Physiological reactions to medications that affect cerebral perfusion pressure.

label: Monitoring Time in Red Zone
definition: The percentage of monitoring time during which intracranial pressure exceeds a defined intensity threshold, associated with worse outcomes.

label: Upper Good Recovery
definition: An outcome category in the Glasgow Outcome Scale representing complete or near-complete recovery.

label: Lower Good Recovery
definition: An outcome category in the Glasgow Outcome Scale representing good recovery with minor deficits.

label: Conservative Management
definition: Non-surgical medical treatment approach for conditions like intracerebral hemorrhage.

label: Vegetative State
definition: A severe disorder of consciousness where patients are awake but show no awareness of self or environment.

label: Head Injury
definition: An injury to the head, mentioned as a condition where hypotension duration is a prognostic factor.

label: Cerebrovascular Autoregulation
definition: The brain's ability to maintain constant blood flow despite changes in perfusion pressure, assessed by pressure reactivity index.

label: Second-tier Therapies
definition: Intermediate-level interventions in the stepped management of severe traumatic brain injury, typically employed when first-tier treatments are insufficient.

label: Warning Time
definition: The time interval by which a predictive system provides early warning before the onset of a clinical event such as hypotension.

label: Vital Signs Monitoring Data
definition: Continuous physiological data such as heart rate and blood pressure, monitored in ICU settings and checked for artifacts.

label: Two Unreactive Pupils
definition: A pupil abnormality where both pupils are non-reactive to light.

label: Phase Ii Study
definition: A repeat clinical study phase to further evaluate predictive models using modified methodologies.

label: Brain Trauma Foundation Guideline
definition: Evidence-based clinical guidelines for the management of traumatic brain injury, including monitoring and treatment thresholds.

label: ICP Insult
definition: An episode defined by a certain intracranial pressure intensity threshold and a certain duration threshold, associated with patient outcome.

label: General Anesthesia
definition: A state of controlled unconsciousness induced by drugs for surgical procedures, associated with risks such as hypotension.

label: Artifactual Events
definition: Non-physiological artifacts or noise in monitoring data that need to be detected to ensure data quality.

label: Ischaemic Mechanism
definition: A pathological process leading to reduced blood flow, contributing to high intracranial pressure and brain swelling.

label: Admission Glasgow Coma Scale
definition: A neurological assessment scale used to evaluate the level of consciousness in patients upon admission, typically after traumatic brain injury.

label: First-tier Treatment
definition: Initial standard interventions for managing traumatic brain injury including head elevation, sedation, and temperature control.

label: Sex
definition: A demographic variable representing the patient's sex, used as an input feature in clinical studies.

label: Non-evacuated Mass Lesions
definition: Intracranial mass lesions that are not surgically removed, classified under the Marshall classification system.

label: Modified Glasgow Outcome Score
definition: An adapted version of the Glasgow Outcome Score used specifically for paediatric patients to assess functional outcome.

label: Admission Pupil Reactivity
definition: A clinical assessment of pupil response to light upon patient admission, used as a baseline risk factor in neurological evaluation.

label: Extended Glasgow Outcome Score
definition: An 8-point scale assessing functional recovery and disability at six months following traumatic brain injury.

label: Admission Motor Glasgow Coma Scale
definition: The motor component of the Glasgow Coma Scale assessed upon admission, used as a core variable in outcome prediction models.

label: Severe Head Trauma
definition: A traumatic brain injury of high severity, often monitored in intensive care settings for secondary insults and outcomes.

label: Head Up Position
definition: A patient positioning intervention, specifically at 30 degrees, used in neurocritical care to manage intracranial pressure.

label: Phase I Study
definition: An initial clinical study phase to test data acquisition and prediction software in a live environment.

label: Pragmatic Clinical Setting
definition: A real-world healthcare environment where interventions are applied as part of routine clinical practice, as opposed to controlled trial conditions.

label: Severe Disability
definition: A functional outcome category where patients require assistance with daily activities.

label: Lower Severe Disability
definition: An outcome category in the Glasgow Outcome Scale representing severe disability requiring assistance.

label: Lower Moderate Disability
definition: An outcome category in the Glasgow Outcome Scale representing moderate disability with limitations.

label: End-hourly Data
definition: Physiological monitoring data recorded at the end of each hour in traumatic brain injury patients.

label: Electronic Health Record
definition: Digital versions of patient health information, often integrated with monitoring data in critical care.

label: Episodic Data
definition: Data including treatments given, lab results from routine blood samples, and nursing procedures.

label: Median Intracranial Hypoperfusion Index 60
definition: The median percentage of monitoring time with cerebral perfusion pressure below 60 mmHg.

label: Mortality
definition: The rate of death occurring during a patient's hospital stay, which can increase with delays in treating hypotension.

label: Insult Grading (EUSIG)
definition: A system for grading secondary insults, including hypotensive events, in neurocritical care patients.

label: Impact Model Core Variables
definition: Key prognostic variables used in the IMPACT model for traumatic brain injury, including age, admission motor Glasgow Coma Scale, and pupil reactivity.

label: Admission Time to Icu
definition: The time point when a patient is admitted to the intensive care unit, considered as a parameter in predictive modeling.

label: EUSIG Grade
definition: A physiological adverse event scoring system used to define and record arterial hypotension events.

label: Severely Disabled
definition: A neurological outcome indicating significant functional impairment, corresponding to GOS scores 1-3.

label: TBI Guidelines
definition: Clinical practice guidelines for the management of severe traumatic brain injury, including recommendations for cerebral perfusion pressure targets.

label: Road Traffic Accident Injury
definition: A type of traumatic injury resulting from road traffic accidents, categorized as a main cause of traumatic brain injury in the patient cohort.

label: Atrium Height
definition: The anatomical level of the heart's atria, used as a reference point for blood pressure transducer placement.

label: Admission Data
definition: Clinical data collected at hospital admission used for prognostic modeling in traumatic brain injury.

label: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage
definition: A type of stroke caused by bleeding within the brain parenchyma, sometimes treated surgically.

label: Dynamic Linear Model
definition: A statistical model designed to detect specific types of artifacts in clinical data, such as those from arterial pressure lines.

label: Distributed Clinical Data
definition: Clinical data collected from multiple sources or sites, used for predictive modeling of adverse events like hypotension.

label: IMPACT Core Model
definition: A prognostic scoring model for traumatic brain injury that predicts mortality and unfavorable outcome.

label: Abandoned Event
definition: A recorded event in a monitoring system that was active but subsequent readings lacked valid measurements, potentially indicating lost data.

label: TIL Score 2
definition: Therapy Intensity Level score 2 indicating moderate-intensity ICP-lowering therapy.

label: Autoregulation Capacity
definition: The ability of cerebral blood vessels to maintain constant blood flow despite changes in perfusion pressure.

label: Prognostic Models
definition: Statistical models used to predict clinical outcomes in traumatic brain injury patients.

label: Pedestrian Injury
definition: A type of traumatic injury involving pedestrians, categorized under injury causes in the patient cohort.

label: Invalid Event
definition: A recorded event that completed but had missing time blocks of data, affecting detection accuracy.

label: Gender
definition: A demographic and baseline risk factor considered in patient assessment and outcome prediction models.

label: Multidisciplinary Consensus
definition: A collaborative decision-making process involving multiple healthcare professionals, such as neurosurgeons and neuro-intensivists, to determine patient care plans.

label: Discriminative Switching Linear Dynamical System Model
definition: A model developed to automatically detect artifacts like arterial pressure line interruptions or damping events in physiological data.

label: Upper Moderate Disability
definition: An outcome category in the Glasgow Outcome Scale representing moderate disability with good function.

label: Artifactual Data
definition: Invalid or non-physiological data in clinical measurements caused by artifacts such as patient movement or equipment issues.

label: 6-month Unfavourable Outcome
definition: An unfavourable neurological outcome assessed at 6 months after traumatic brain injury.

label: Third-tier Therapies
definition: Advanced interventions in the management of severe traumatic brain injury, including surgical options like decompressive craniectomy, used when lower-tier treatments fail.

label: Six-months Outcome
definition: Clinical outcome assessed at six months following traumatic brain injury.

label: IMPACT Extended Model
definition: An extended version of the IMPACT prognostic model incorporating additional variables.

label: TIL Score 4
definition: Therapy Intensity Level score 4 indicating maximal medical ICP-lowering therapy.

label: IMPACT Lab Model
definition: A laboratory-based version of the IMPACT prognostic model incorporating biochemical variables.

label: TIL Score 0
definition: Therapy Intensity Level score 0 indicating minimal ICP-lowering therapy.

label: TIL Score 1
definition: Therapy Intensity Level score 1 indicating low-intensity ICP-lowering therapy.

label: Quality of Life
definition: A multidimensional concept encompassing physical, psychological, and social well-being, used as an outcome measure in clinical studies.

label: Insult Grading Classification
definition: A classification system, such as EUSIG, used to analyze and grade clinical insults like hypotension events from patient data.

label: Hyperosmolar Molecules
definition: Medications administered as second-tier treatment to reduce cerebral edema and intracranial pressure.

label: Upper Severe Disability
definition: An outcome category in the Glasgow Outcome Scale representing severe disability with some independence.

label: CRASH Prognostic Model
definition: A prognostic scoring system for traumatic brain injury predicting 14-day mortality and 6-month unfavorable outcome.

label: Refractory Cases
definition: Instances of a medical condition that do not respond to standard treatments, often requiring advanced or aggressive interventions.

label: TIL Score 3
definition: Therapy Intensity Level score 3 indicating high-intensity ICP-lowering therapy.

label: Age
definition: A demographic and baseline risk factor considered in patient assessment and outcome prediction models.
